items.text: From 31 January 2020, adults 18 and over in the ACT aren't committing an offence by possessing up to 50 g of dried cannabis (150 g harvested but not dried), or by growing one or two plants, as long as they're not grown artificially. More than four plants at one home, and smoking cannabis in a public place or near a child, are offences.

laws.rule: Parks ACT says dogs are not allowed in Namadgi National Park or the adjoining Gibraltar Forest Regeneration Area. Dogs may remain in vehicles travelling between the ACT and NSW on Boboyan or Brindabella roads.

laws.rule: Parks ACT says drones are not permitted to be used in Namadgi National Park. This rule is for Namadgi and does not establish rules for every ACT reserve.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: If you find an Aboriginal heritage object or place in the ACT, do not move it, do not do anything that might damage it, and alert ACT Heritage at heritage@act.gov.au within 5 working days. In parks and reserves, leave cultural sites undisturbed. At Yankee Hat in Namadgi National Park, do not touch the rock art or the rock surface, because oils from skin will damage the painting.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Parks and reserves are on Ngunnawal Country. There are more than 1,400 recorded Aboriginal heritage sites in ACT parks and reserves, including stone artefact scatters, rock shelters, scarred trees and sacred sites. Heritage places and objects are protected under the Heritage Act 2004, and additionally under the Nature Conservation Act 2014 where they are in reserves. It is an offence to damage, disturb or destroy Aboriginal heritage places including objects. The Namadgi visitor guide also asks visitors not to collect, deface or damage Aboriginal or European cultural heritage artefacts or sites.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Ngunnawal Traditional Custodians; ACT Heritage; ACT Parks and Conservation Service.
culture-and-protocol.note: Statewide ACT Government and Parks ACT guidance, plus the official Yankee Hat and Namadgi visitor guides for the rock-art and leave-undisturbed rules.
